inline:The target misidentifies the single best cross-city modulator of the nocturnal UHI gap by privileging sky view factor (SVF) over stored sensible heat release, which it concedes is the dominant mechanism in its own counterconditions.
The target commits to assessing which single mechanism best explains why the night-time gap is larger in some cities than in others. It nominates SVF, describing it as the 'single best cross-city modulator.' However, in its counterconditions and mechanism text, the target concedes that stored sensible heat release actually dominates the nocturnal energy budget. If stored heat release dominates the nocturnal energy budget (as the target admits), it is inconsistent to claim SVF is the 'single best' modulator of the magnitude of that nighttime gap. The storage and release of sensible heat in urban thermal mass is the primary cited reason the air stays warmer at night and varies by city. SVF only modulates radiative cooling efficiency, which is secondary to the massive energy flux from daytime heat storage. This internal contradiction overturns the target's central claim.
